summary: A contractor is the consumer of the materials it incorporates into real property and pays the tax; the customer's construction or repair contract isn't taxed.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2015-21 (December 16, 2015), Contractors
citations.quote: A contractor is the per se end user and consumer of tangible personal property purchased for use in performing contracts, and such property is not considered to be purchased by the contractor for resale.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2015-21 (December 16, 2015), Contractors
citations.quote: Taxpayer is not required to collect the tax from the customer on any components of the contract

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2019-05 (July 16, 2019), Contractors; sign construction, installation
citations.quote: Charges made by Taxpayer for either the installation or repair of a sign incorporated into real property are not subject to sales and use tax.

notes: Covers improvement and repair. Letter rulings bind only their requesters; they apply O.C.G.A. § 48-8-63.

summary: Delivery charges on taxable goods are part of the sales price and taxable, even if optional or separately stated.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2016-04 (February 15, 2016), Sales Price - Delivery Charges
citations.quote: When a seller of taxable tangible personal property makes a delivery charge to the customer, sales tax applies to the delivery charge.

citations.title: Georgia DOR, What is Subject to Sales and Use Tax?
citations.quote: Charges made for delivery, transportation, freight, or shipping and handling are part of the sales price and subject to sales tax in the same manner as the underlying sale.

summary: Retail sales of tangible personal property are taxable at the 4% state rate plus local taxes.

citations.title: Georgia DOR, What is Subject to Sales and Use Tax?
citations.quote: In general, Georgia imposes tax on the retail sales price of tangible personal property and certain services.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2019-05 (July 16, 2019), Contractors; sign construction, installation
citations.quote: Georgia levies and imposes a tax (subject to certain specific exemptions) on the retail purchase, retail sale, storage, use, or consumption of tangible personal property

notes: Local sales taxes share the state base for this code.

summary: Georgia taxes only enumerated services; professional, consulting, IT, design and advertising services aren't among them.

citations.title: Georgia DOR, What is Subject to Sales and Use Tax?
citations.quote: While most services are exempt from tax, Georgia does tax the sale of accommodations, in-state transportation of individuals (e.g., taxis, limos), sales of admissions, and charges for participation in games and amusement activities.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2016-09 (March 30, 2016), Software and Software Related
citations.quote: sales of services are not subject to the tax unless the service is specifically designated as taxable

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2014-15 (October 17, 2014), Service Provider - Information Technology Services
citations.quote: Thus as a general rule, service providers, in the same manner as contractors, are end users and consumers of the tangible personal property used to provide their services and are liable for the tax on all such property.

notes: Applies to every professional subcode. A service provider's own sales of tangible goods (e.g. an interior decorator selling furnishings) are taxable sales of goods.

summary: Prewritten software is taxable on a tangible medium and not taxed when delivered only electronically.

conditions.when: Delivered in a tangible medium, or the buyer also receives (or has a right to) a tangible copy

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2016-09 (March 30, 2016), Software and Software Related
citations.quote: Computer software delivered electronically is not a sale of tangible personal property and therefore is not subject to sales or use tax.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2016-09 (March 30, 2016), Software and Software Related
citations.quote: If a dealer delivers computer software electronically and also provides the same software to the purchaser in a tangible medium, the transaction is a taxable sale of tangible personal property.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2024-02 (November 25, 2024), prewritten computer software
citations.quote: The sale of prewritten computer software sold in a tangible medium is taxable unless otherwise exempt.

summary: Remotely accessed software is not a sale of tangible personal property or an enumerated taxable service, so it isn't taxed.

citations.title: Georgia DOR Letter Ruling LR SUT-2016-09 (March 30, 2016), Software and Software Related

notes: Rule 560-12-2-.118 (digital products, 2024) reportedly lists software as a service among exempt items; its text wasn't read (the DOR copy was unavailable).
